title: GUI Development for SSDL to Calibrate Photon Measuring Equipment
author: Belhaj, Belhaj, et al.

steps.title: Perform initial instrument checks
steps.instruction: When a survey meter arrives, carry out operational checks: verify battery condition, perform a radiation‑response check, and confirm the zero reading.

steps.title: Set up calibration geometry
steps.instruction: Select the appropriate radioactive source (γ‑ray) or beam quality (X‑ray) based on the required energy range, choose the calibration point, place the reference standard at the centre of the beam, and install attenuators that cover the survey meter’s measurement range. The laboratory uses the substitution (method 4) approach.

steps.title: Measure air Kerma with reference standard
steps.instruction: Using the reference standard, measure the air Kerma (Kair) at the calibration reference point. Apply corrections for air temperature, air pressure, polarity and recombination. Record the Kair display at least five times at regular intervals and calculate the average value.

steps.title: Convert Kair to H*(10)
steps.instruction: Convert the averaged Kair to the radiation‑protection quantity H*(10) (or Hp(10)) by applying the ISO 4037‑3 conversion coefficient appropriate for the source spectrum. If a 3‑mm PMMA build‑up plate is used, multiply the conversion coefficient by the correction factor kPMMA (kPMMA = 1 for ¹³⁷Cs and ⁶⁰Co).

steps.title: Prepare survey meter for exposure
steps.instruction: Adjust the survey meter to the appropriate exposure/dose range, place a 3‑mm PMMA build‑up plate in front of its detector when secondary‑electron equilibrium is required, and position the meter at the calibrated source‑beam distance (the calibration point). Verify that the meter is centred in the beam and record a background reading with the beam off.

steps.title: Expose meter and record readings
steps.instruction: Expose the survey meter to the radiation field, record its display at least five times at regular intervals, and compute the average reading, the standard deviation, and the standard uncertainty.

steps.title: Calculate calibration factor
steps.instruction: Calculate the calibration factor CF using CF = H/M, where H is the true H*(10) value obtained in step 4 and M is the average instrument reading from step 6. Verify that the relative deviation of the instrument from the reference ionisation chamber is within ±30 % of the expected dose‑rate.

steps.title: Perform distance‑dependence test (X‑ray only)
steps.instruction: For X‑ray calibrations, after the initial measurement, move the survey meter to distances 2×, 3×, 4×, 5×, 6× and 7× the calibration distance, record the reading at each distance, plot distance versus measured radiation (inverse‑square law), extrapolate the expected value back to the calibration distance, and recalculate the calibration factor.

steps.title: Repeat for all required ranges
steps.instruction: Repeat the entire procedure for each exposure or dose‑rate range (γ‑ray) or for each radiation quality (X‑ray) required by the calibration programme.
